summary: Missionary Ridge observation tower (1890s), taken apart and moved to Fall Creek Falls State Park in 1941 or 1943; the moved tower still stands there.

facts.status_note: Missionary Ridge tower was taken apart and moved; the reassembled tower stands at Fall Creek Falls State Park, Bledsoe County

events.note: Observation tower on Missionary Ridge per tnlandforms (75 ft). NRHP nomination says constructed ca. 1895; NHLR says originally built 1865. Sources disagree.
Declared unsafe and in need of repair or removal; visitors no longer allowed to climb it
Decision to raze in 1941; local push to save it led to disassembly and transfer to Fall Creek Falls by CCC workers. Tnlandforms and NHLR give 1943 for the move.
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register as Fall Creek Falls Lookout Tower
National Register record NRIS 15000444 for Fall Creek Falls Fire Lookout Tower, asset dated 7/21/2015

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Braggs entry on Missionary Ridge and the Fall Creek Falls tower are one structure: the tnlandforms catalog and the NRHP nomination both say it was moved from Missionary Ridge to Fall Creek Falls. The story covers both sites.
Hamilton County is the original site; the reassembled tower is in Bledsoe County

notes_for_editor: Record covers the original Missionary Ridge site (35.0193, -85.2634, Hamilton County). The reassembled tower is at Fall Creek Falls State Park. Coordinates and elevations for that tower do not agree: tnlandforms BLT002 gives 35.6696, -85.3059 at 2018 ft; NHLR gives 35.657250, -85.347900 at 1,713 ft; the NRHP nomination gives 2,026 ft. A separate record for the Fall Creek tower may be worth making once that is checked. Dates disagree: built 1865 (NHLR), 1893 (tnlandforms), ca. 1895 (NRHP); moved 1941 (NRHP) vs 1943 (tnlandforms, NHLR). The NHLR 1865 date is out of line with the other two, but no source here settles it. Height: facts.height_m uses the 75 ft original figure from tnlandforms; the reassembled tower is described as 80 ft in the nomination. The Chattanooga Public Library record that turned up in search sits behind a bot-check page and was not used. The NHLR lists the Tennessee Division of Forestry as a cooperator; the agency fact follows the NHLR administering line. No source describes Missionary Ridge today.
